title: The Arctic opens
hook: Melting ice is creating a new ocean, and new claims.
notes: September Arctic sea-ice minimum ≈ 7 million km² around 1980 vs ≈ 3.4 million in 2012 (record low), NSIDC. Ice is drawn as a circle of equal area, schematic. Routes schematic; distances computed along the drawn line.

scenes.title: Looking down from the pole
scenes.text: Most maps cut the Arctic into an edge. On a globe it is the centre of a ring of powers: Russia, the US, Canada, Denmark via Greenland, Norway.

scenes.title: The ice is shrinking
scenes.text: Around 1980, September sea ice covered about 7 million km². In 2012 it fell to about 3.4 million. Each circle has the same area as the ice in that year.

scenes.title: A shortcut to Asia
scenes.text: The Northern Sea Route along Russia's coast is far shorter between Europe and East Asia than the route via Suez. Ice, cost and politics still keep most ships away.

scenes.title: The Northwest Passage
scenes.text: On the Canadian side, a maze of islands. Canada calls these internal waters; the US and others call it an international strait.

scenes.title: Who owns the pole
scenes.text: Russia, Denmark and Canada have all filed UN claims to the seabed of the Lomonosov Ridge. Their claims overlap, and all three include the North Pole.
